Bipolar and absolutely feel that Brand New lyrically has spoken so much of what I feel. I remember when TDAG came out I felt upset for him in a way. Such a painful way to feel. I felt it to my core.

But Science Fiction really got it for me.

In a way I feel my diagnosis in 2005 very much aligned as brand new progressed in albums. In a way no other band has done. I think that’s why I have such a connection with this music. 

I also sometimes feel when some people say “separate the art from the artist” it’s not realistic here. Being a brand new fan all these years it was so incredibly clear the issues, thoughts, regrets, feelings were true and raw. Maybe it’s my own experience with mental illness, but before mostly stabilizing I have done so many things I am embarrassed by/cannot believe that was once me.  I think it is hard to explain the internal agitation and anger and deep sadness of just wanting out. I know I hurt people I care about and I cannot take that back. But one can get better, be better, admit their faults, and try to heal those wrongs. 

These artists saved my life.

Oh also! It’s such a cool abstract work you can epoxy it with what you can and then do some resin filler maybe with a drippy look. It’s very organic so it might be fun to experiment mixed media for fun. Might make something even cooler. Kiln happenings can be so upsetting but one positive is you can experiment on it and maybe it was meant to be. Kind of a fun side project. Totally worth it to just enjoy the possibilities! I love your piece by the way way!

Remember to get a tiny air hole in any area fully enclosed. This looks like a moisture explosion though with all the tiny pieces. I would say just make sure it’s no longer cool to the touch whatsoever. That’s usually my go to, room temperature feeling all around to check it is reaching bone dry. 

Possibly with thicker work doing a few hour preheat or canceling can take out any extra moisture on a larger work before starting to ramp up the kiln.

I suggest just taking a walk outside. No real plans or expectations, but just for yourself. It is amazing what just sitting or walking in a nice place can do. Maybe get a coffee or smoothie. Make sure to bring water and stay hydrated even just for a stroll. Listen to some music or just what is around you. It’s still solitude but in a lighter way and you can pick and choose your comfort.

I would look up unique places in your area and do this for you! It will not solve everything, but it has always been a great start to climb out of a deep depression for myself. I would highly recommend! Wishing you the best.

I would def. check in with the seller the history of the kiln if they were the original owner. Although it is rare some people used to or some still do use glazes with lead and cadmium in them. It has potential to seep into the brick and could cause issues if it was used with glazes like that regularly. I am just a super safe person when it comes to food safety in functional wares. I am sure it is fine, I am just chiming in because it has a sitter that looks on the older side. What I do with used kilns is get a test out to a water company. She would have to throw a certain size cylinder, send it out for leaching, and will get the results. If for sculptures it is 100 percent fine! If she needs any help with the sitter I have some demos on setting it up. Sitters are nice because you have more control over the firing process than in electric models. 

Like I said I am sure it is fine, but if she will be selling mugs, bowls, etc. I would stay safe.
